prompt: What is a vSphere Standard Switch (vSS)?
options: A software Layer-2 switch within an ESXi host
A DNS server that assigns host names
A hardware router installed inside every VM
A datastore that stores virtual disks
en: A vSS connects compatible virtual interfaces and can use uplinks for external connectivity.
ru: vSS compatible virtual interfaces connect karta aur bahar ke liye uplinks use kar sakta hai.

prompt: Which object provides the ESXi host’s IP-enabled interface for management?
options: A VMkernel adapter such as vmk0
The vSwitch name itself
The VM’s virtual disk
The physical switch’s power supply
en: The management IP belongs to a VMkernel interface, not the standard switch object.
ru: Management IP VMkernel interface ka hota hai, standard switch object ka nahin.

prompt: What is an uplink in standard-switch networking?
options: An ESXi vmnic assigned to provide an external network path
A DNS suffix attached to a host name
A secondary virtual disk for a VM
A guest operating system’s default password
en: The uplink joins the virtual switch to a suitable network beyond its local switching domain.
ru: Uplink virtual switch ko uske local switching domain se bahar munasib network se jorta hai.

prompt: What connects a guest VM’s virtual network adapter to an ESXi standard-switch network?
options: A virtual-machine port group
The ESXi hosts file
A DNS reverse zone
The datastore browser
en: A guest vNIC attaches to a VM port group on the switch.
ru: Guest vNIC switch ke VM port group se attach hota hai.

prompt: Who normally manages the configuration of a standard switch?
options: Each ESXi host individually
Only a DNS primary server
Every guest VM independently
A single shared Windows hosts file
en: A vSS is host-specific; distributed-switch management follows a different model.
ru: vSS host-specific hai; distributed switch management alag model hai.

prompt: What is the role of a port group?
options: Group virtual ports under common connection and policy settings
Assign a public DNS domain automatically
Convert every VM into a router
Store guest operating-system files
en: Port groups provide network attachment and policy context, not application storage or DNS registration.
ru: Port groups network attachment aur policy context dete hain, application storage ya DNS registration nahin.

prompt: Can a standard switch exist without a physical uplink?
options: Yes; compatible local endpoints can still communicate within the host
No; ESXi automatically deletes every uplink-free switch
Only when every VM is powered off
Only if it becomes a DNS server
en: An uplink is required for an external path, not for every local exchange.
ru: Uplink external path ke liye hai, har local exchange ke liye nahin.

prompt: Does a basic standard switch route between different IP subnets by itself?
options: No; inter-subnet connectivity requires suitable routing elsewhere
Yes; every new port group becomes a router
Yes; changing the switch name enables routing
Only if DNS resolves the destination
en: A vSS provides Layer-2 switching; routing is a different function.
ru: vSS Layer-2 switching deta hai; routing alag function hai.

prompt: What does a reported 10000 Full link indicate?
options: A reported 10 Gbit/s full-duplex link property
Measured 10 Gbit/s Internet throughput
Guaranteed 10 Gbit/s for each application
Proof that all failover tests passed
en: Reported link characteristics are not end-to-end throughput measurements.
ru: Reported link characteristics end-to-end throughput measurements nahin.

prompt: What does a nested ESXi vmnic often represent?
options: A virtualized hardware NIC presented by the outer hypervisor
Always a dedicated physical PCI card in the desktop
A Windows DNS zone file
The guest VM’s storage controller
en: Workstation can present virtual NIC hardware to nested ESXi.
ru: Workstation nested ESXi ko virtual NIC hardware present kar sakta hai.

prompt: The recorded ESXi9 topology shows vmk0 at 10.0.0.10 on Management Network. Which object owns that IP?
options: vmk0
vSwitch0 itself
The SERVERS label
Every VM on VM Network
en: The IP endpoint is the host VMkernel interface.
ru: IP endpoint host ka VMkernel interface hai.

prompt: Two same-host VMs share a compatible Layer-2 network and policies allow communication. The external uplink is down. What can still work?
options: Their local communication through the vSwitch
Every Internet connection through the failed uplink
A guaranteed path to every remote host
Only communication routed through the failed physical cable
en: Same-host switching may remain local and does not need the external uplink for that exchange.
ru: Same-host switching local reh sakti hai aur us exchange ke liye external uplink nahin chahiye.

prompt: A VM needs to reach a physical peer on the same intended LAN. What is required beyond its local vNIC and port group?
options: A working compatible uplink and upstream network path
Only a different display name for the port group
Only a larger virtual disk
A DNS alias regardless of network reachability
en: An external destination requires an actual path beyond the ESXi switch.
ru: External destination ke liye ESXi switch se bahar actual path chahiye.

prompt: SERVERS and VM Network both use the same untagged Layer-2 network. Do different labels alone isolate their traffic?
options: No; names alone do not create isolation
Yes; every name creates a unique VLAN
Yes; a label automatically enables a firewall
Only labels written in uppercase create isolation
en: Segmentation depends on network/policy design, not merely the group label.
ru: Segmentation network/policy design par depend karti hai, sirf group label par nahin.

prompt: A snapshot shows SERVERS created with zero attached VMs. What is established?
options: The port group exists; guest connectivity remains untested
Every server guest has passed a ping test
All VMs automatically moved into SERVERS
The network is definitely faulty because no VM is attached
en: Configuration existence and guest traffic verification are separate claims.
ru: Configuration ka hona aur guest traffic verification alag claims hain.

prompt: vmnic1 must move from vSwitch0 to another standard switch. What constraint matters?
options: A vmnic cannot belong to two standard switches simultaneously
A vmnic must always have a DNS A record first
The second switch must use the same name as the first
The host must delete every VM before any NIC assignment change
en: Its current switch membership must be handled before reassigning it.
ru: Reassign karne se pehle uski current switch membership handle hoti hai.

prompt: A screen shows vmnic0 and vmnic1 assigned to a switch. Which claim requires additional testing?
options: Automatic failover works during a real link failure
Two uplinks are shown in that captured configuration
The switch has those listed memberships at that time
The screenshot identifies two adapter names
en: Membership alone does not prove policy behavior or upstream path redundancy.
ru: Membership akeli policy behavior ya upstream redundancy prove nahin karti.

prompt: The earlier screenshot shows one uplink; a later inventory shows two. How should the notes describe them?
options: As separate historical checkpoints, with live state verified before changes
Treat the oldest image as the permanent final state
Assume the later image proves every uncaptured intermediate step
Delete one observation because they cannot both have occurred
en: Configuration changes over time; historical evidence needs chronology.
ru: Configuration waqt ke saath badalti hai; historical evidence ko chronology chahiye.

prompt: A standard switch named STORAGE is created. Does its name alone prove a working storage datastore?
options: No; storage endpoint and protocol/datastore tests are separate
Yes; the name automatically mounts NFS
Yes; ESXi creates an iSCSI target from the label
Only if the name contains an uppercase letter
en: Network objects do not automatically establish storage sessions or mount datastores.
ru: Network objects automatically storage sessions ya datastores mount nahin karte.

prompt: You want to inspect existing standard switches and uplinks without changing them. Which shell command fits?
options: esxcli network vswitch standard list
esxcli system shutdown poweroff
esxcli storage filesystem unmount
esxcli network vswitch standard remove -v vSwitch0
en: The list command inventories standard-switch configuration.
ru: List command standard-switch configuration ki inventory deta hai.

prompt: Local same-host VM traffic works, but external traffic fails. Which area is especially relevant?
options: Uplink assignment/status and the outer/upstream network path
Only the datastore file names
Assume local success proves the external cable works
Only the browser bookmark title
en: The local path may bypass the uplink, so external failure needs separate path checks.
ru: Local path uplink bypass kar sakta hai; external failure ke path checks alag hain.

prompt: A management VLAN or uplink change disconnects remote access. What recovery preparation is most valuable?
options: Working local console access and a recorded rollback configuration
An unrelated DNS MX record
A renamed desktop shortcut
A larger VM display resolution
en: Management-network changes can strand the session; console recovery preserves a way back.
ru: Management changes session disconnect kar sakti hain; console recovery wapas access deti hai.

prompt: A free vmnic is absent from the target switch’s selection. What should be checked first?
options: Whether another switch already owns it and whether ESXi sees the adapter
Whether its name is listed in a reverse DNS zone
Whether every VM has the same administrator password
Whether the switch label ends in .com
en: Inventory the actual device and assignment before assuming it is available.
ru: Available assume karne se pehle actual device aur assignment inspect karein.

prompt: A nested uplink reports connected, but the external test endpoint is unreachable. What check is useful?
options: Match its MAC to the Workstation NIC and verify the outer network mapping
Assume link-up proves all upstream paths are correct
Change every storage MTU to 9000 without testing
Delete the management interface first
en: A connected virtual link can still lead to the wrong outer network.
ru: Connected virtual link phir bhi ghalat outer network tak ja sakta hai.

prompt: A student uses a successful same-host ping as proof of uplink failover. What is missing?
options: An external traffic path with controlled link fault and observed recovery
A different color for the port group label
A CNAME for every physical NIC
A second DNS suffix on the client
en: A local ping may never traverse an uplink, so it cannot establish that uplink’s failover.
ru: Local ping uplink par ja hi na sakti ho; is se us uplink ka failover prove nahin.
